bullets: HCP Terraform now sends notification emails when API tokens are nearing expiration (30 days and 7 days.
Fixed the display of workspace and project counts in policy set summaries and indexes when the policy set is not a Terraform Policy VCS policy set.
The add_team and remove_team project audit events now include team_id, team_name, permissions, and project_name, ensuring historical records remain reliable even if team names change.

An Actions dropdown is now available, providing options for Select All, Reset Selection, and Bulk Delete. A warning message and delete confirmation modal have been added to prevent accidental deletions.
Manage team tokens with bulk deletion and filters for active, expired, expiring in 7 or 30 days, and no expiration.

Tags are now a valid scope for a policy set. Use matching logic of 'And'/'Or' to specify whether all or just one of the specified tags should be present on a workspace for it to be targeted by a policy set.
Terraform policy can now evaluate policies against Stacks. Evaluations are triggered during a deployment run, and occur post-plan.

The Teams page now includes an "ID" copy link, allowing you to easily copy the team ID for use in other workflows. This addition enhances the usability of the Teams page by providing a quick and convenient way to access the team ID.
Enhanced team management and auditability with team descriptions and richer, persistent audit metadata across organizations, memberships, permissions, teams, projects, and variable sets..
HCP Terraform expands identity lifecycle management and auditability with SCIM provisioning and richer audit metadata for authentication tokens and SAML configuration changes.

HCP Terraform now supports Azure DevOps Org scoped Personal Access Tokens, allowing users to connect using tokens scoped to a specific organization, rather than globally. This change enables users to migrate their VCS connections before Microsoft retires global PATs on December 1, 2026.
For Flex 1.0 billing accounts, the **Premium plan now appears as a locked card** beside Essentials and Standard, so it cannot be selected. Other organizations can still select Premium.

**Vault 2.0.3 is now available for HCP Vault** Dedicated clusters on AWS and Azure. Refer to the Vault 2.0.3 release notes to learn more about the new features, enhancements, and fixes included in Vault 2.0.3
**Connectivity Tester:** HCP Vault Dedicated clusters on AWS and Azure now support a connectivity tester that validates network connectivity between the cluster and external endpoints.

**Vault 2.0.4:** Vault 2.0.4 is now available for HCP Vault Dedicated clusters on AWS and Azure. Refer to the Vault 2.0.4 release notes to learn more about the new features, enhancements, and fixes included in Vault 2.0.4.
**Data plane account details:** HCP Vault Dedicated clusters on AWS and Azure now expose the data plane account details directly..

**Vault 2.1.2 addresses CVE-2026-105818**, a PKI secrets engine vulnerability that could allow unverified identities in certificates issued through the default ACME directory policy. Manual-upgrade clusters should upgrade as soon as possible.
Focuses on security hardening, addressing vulnerabilities and strengthening content boundary enforcement for VCS-based module ingestion, including remediation for CVE-2026-14468

Delivers targeted reliability, identity and integration improvements, addressing SCIM synchronization with Microsoft Entra ID, GitHub Enterprise Cloud workflows, private registry processing, and security vulnerabilities.

Focused maintenance release that improves operational flexibility and platform reliability, while strengthening security and addressing issues across VCS operations, Terraform Stacks, Explorer, and multi-architecture deployments.
Strengthens VCS integrations and Terraform 1.15 compatibility while improving drift detection, connectivity, and overall platform security.
Improves deployment reliability by fixing Sidekiq startup failures when using a separate Redis instance with mTLS and password authentication.

Added a "**Submit feedback" button** to the sidebar navigation and the Help and Support dropdown, linking to an external feedback survey.

Containers: Remove cap_ipc_lock capability on vault at build time Runtime operators are advised to disable swapping to guarantee data safety.
secrets/ssh: RSA key sizes are now limited to a maximum size of 8192 bits addressing CVE-2026-39829
**Introduces native support for AI agents** (public beta), extending Vault's machine identity and secrets management capabilities to emerging AI-driven workloads.
**Operational and user experience improvements** include enhanced Cloud Foundry authentication efficiency, refreshed usage dashboards, and UI stability enhancements.

Expands Vault’s machine identity capabilities with **native AI-agent support**, while delivering targeted reliability, operational and UX improvements and continuing to strengthen the platform’s security posture
**Agentic IAM reaches General Availability**, extending Vault’s machine identity and security capabilities to AI agents and emerging agentic workloads.
**Expanded OAuth support**, policy flexibility, and platform improvements enhance the security, reliability, and operational experience of Vault
**Strengthens secrets import and identity integrations** with trusted private endpoint controls for AWS/Azure imports and enhanced Okta group retrieval for JWT/OIDC authentication.

The release also **expands PKI flexibility** by supporting additional CSR subject attributes, while delivering security patches and fixes across Secrets Sync, Agent Registry, leases, and the Vault UI.

**Vault 2.2.0 adds OAuth2 access tokens for Azure static roles** and generally available SCIM provisioning. It also includes KV v2 snapshot recovery, EdDSA support and a public beta of Vault Client, along with bug fixes.
